sections.section_title: 1. Clinical Presentation and Prior Therapeutic History
sections.description: This section introduces the patient, outlines his symptomatology, comorbidities, and details each previous aortic valve intervention, including the initial TAVI, the first valve‑in‑valve, and the episode of prosthetic valve endocarditis. It establishes the clinical context that led to the need for a third transcatheter intervention.
subtopics: Demographics and presenting symptoms (dyspnoea, chest discomfort, dizziness, fatigue)
Cardiovascular risk profile: hypertension, three‑vessel CAD, prior PCI, AV block with pacemaker
Non‑cardiac comorbidities influencing procedural risk (diabetes, COPD, GI bleeding)
2014 Lotus TAVI: indications, device characteristics, early outcomes
2022 Evolut TAV‑in‑TAV: rationale, procedural complications (femoral pseudo‑aneurysm)
Prosthetic valve endocarditis (Enterococcus faecalis): clinical course, antimicrobial therapy, resolution
Progressive prosthetic degeneration after infection: echocardiographic findings and hemodynamic deterioration

sections.description: Focuses on the multimodality evaluation performed to characterize valve dysfunction, assess anatomic feasibility for another TAVI, and rule out active infection. Emphasizes the role of echocardiography, transoesophageal echo, and especially multidetector CT in planning a TAV‑in‑TAV‑in‑TAV procedure.
subtopics: Transthoracic echocardiography: measurement of gradients, AVA, assessment of regurgitation, detection of double‑layered prostheses
Transoesophageal echo: exclusion of vegetations, paravalvular leaks, and abscess formation
Blood cultures and inflammatory markers: confirming eradication of endocarditis
Multislice CT protocol for redo TAVI: cardiac gating, contrast timing, reconstruction of annular and sinus dimensions
Key CT measurements: annular perimeter, sinus of Valsalva height, coronary ostial distance, frame‑to‑coronary distance, minimum lumen diameter of existing Evolut valve
3‑D modelling and virtual valve implantation: predicting neo‑skirt, commissural alignment, and coronary clearance
Risk assessment for coronary obstruction and patient‑prosthesis mismatch (PPM) using CT‑derived parameters

sections.description: Explains the multidisciplinary heart‑team discussion, risk‑benefit analysis, and the strategic choices that guided the third TAVI, including valve selection, implantation depth, and coronary protection strategies.
subtopics: Surgical risk quantification (EuroSCORE II, frailty, prior surgeries) and why repeat surgery was prohibitive
Indications for a third transcatheter valve: severity of stenosis/regurgitation, symptom burden, and durability expectations
Device selection rationale: Acurate neo2 (supra‑annular leaflets, low frame height, commissural alignment capability)
Alternative strategies considered (valve fracture, BASILICA, surgical explantation) and reasons for exclusion
Pre‑procedural plan for coronary protection: assessment of need vs. CT‑predicted safety
Target implantation depth and alignment strategy to maximize effective orifice area and preserve future coronary access
Balloon sizing and pre‑dilation plan based on CT‑derived minimal lumen diameter
Patient‑specific procedural checklist: anesthesia choice, vascular access strategy, imaging guidance

sections.description: Describes the step‑by‑step conduct of the TAV‑in‑TAV‑in‑TAV procedure, highlighting specific technical challenges unique to a triple‑stented anatomy and how they were overcome.
subtopics: Vascular access selection (left femoral arterial, left radial) and sheath management
Guidewire navigation through two prior valve frames and placement of Safari wire
Balloon pre‑dilation parameters (22 × 40 mm, rapid pacing at 180 bpm) and hemodynamic monitoring
Fluoroscopic and aortographic landmarks used for commissural alignment with the Evolut leaflets
Deployment technique of the Acurate neo2 (positioning, release sequence, verification of depth)
Post‑dilation protocol (20 × 40 mm balloon, rapid pacing) to optimize expansion and reduce PPM
Immediate assessment of coronary flow (angiography) and absence of obstruction
Management of potential complications: valve malposition, coronary occlusion, annular rupture
Documentation of procedural success according to VARC‑3 criteria

sections.section_title: 5. Outcomes, Follow‑up, and Lessons for Lifetime Valve Management
sections.description: Presents short‑ and long‑term clinical and echocardiographic results, evaluates the durability of the triple‑valve construct, and extracts key teaching points for future repeat TAVI cases, especially in the context of prior endocarditis.
subtopics: Immediate post‑procedural echocardiography: gradients, AVA, regurgitation, and detection of severe PPM
Early (1‑month) haemodynamic improvement and left‑ventricular remodeling
Mid‑term (3.5‑month) clinical status: symptom resolution, exercise tolerance, absence of infection
1‑year follow‑up data: mean gradient 26 mm Hg, AVA 1.1 cm², EF 65 %, no regurgitation, no endocarditis recurrence
Analysis of residual PPM and its clinical relevance in a triple‑stented scenario
Implications for coronary access after three overlapping frames and strategies to mitigate future access difficulty
Role of pre‑procedural CT and commissural alignment in achieving favorable outcomes
Guideline context: current ESC/ACC recommendations for TAVI after prosthetic valve endocarditis
Future considerations: bioprosthetic valve fracture, BASILICA, and emerging devices for redo TAVI
Take‑home messages for lifetime management of structural valve disease: early imaging, multidisciplinary planning, and patient‑centred risk stratification
